# Apple Human Interface Guidelines

Use the relevant Apple guidance to make concrete design decisions. This package
contains a router, 13 topic skills, and original article-level references. It is
independent of Apple. The sources are a dated English HIG snapshot; check the
official source when a task depends on a newer release or a disputed detail.

## Route the task

1. Identify the target platform, device context, and user task from the request or
   project. Ask for the platform only when it materially affects the answer and
   cannot be inferred. Preserve the user's framework and product requirements.
2. Select the relevant family below. Read that family's `SKILL.md`, then only the
   article references needed for the task. Nested skills are explicitly read by
   file path; automatic nested discovery is not required.
3. For an exact component, technology, or unfamiliar term, search the
   [complete topic index](references/topic-index.md). It links directly to local
   article references. Do not load the full corpus for a narrow question.
   For a screenshot-specific or animated example, also consult its
   [original visual explanation](references/media/index.md) when available.
4. Apply shared guidance and the target platform's documented differences. A
   missing platform subsection means no additional rule is stated; it does not
   prove support, nonapplicability, or identical behavior across platforms.
5. Compose families when the task crosses them: a component can also require
   accessibility, typography, localization, input, or system-experience guidance.
   Use [platform and task routes](references/platforms-and-tasks.md) when useful.

All paths are relative to **this installed package**, not the shell's current
directory. No Python, network, sibling skill installation, or authoring cache is
required to read the guidance.

| Task | Read this topic skill |
|---|---|
| Platform conventions, design principles, games, device adaptation | [Getting started](subskills/apple-hig-getting-started/SKILL.md) |
| Accessibility, typography, color, materials, layout, localization, privacy | [Foundations](subskills/apple-hig-foundations/SKILL.md) |
| Onboarding, loading, search, sharing, accounts, feedback, media, settings | [Patterns](subskills/apple-hig-patterns/SKILL.md) |
| Charts, images, text views, embedded web content | [Content](subskills/apple-hig-content/SKILL.md) |
| Lists, collections, split views, tab views, disclosure and grouping | [Layout and organization](subskills/apple-hig-layout-and-organization/SKILL.md) |
| Buttons, menus, toolbars, menu bar, ornaments and actions | [Menus and actions](subskills/apple-hig-menus-and-actions/SKILL.md) |
| Sidebars, tab bars, search fields, tokens and path controls | [Navigation and search](subskills/apple-hig-navigation-and-search/SKILL.md) |
| Alerts, sheets, popovers, panels, scrolling and windows | [Presentation](subskills/apple-hig-presentation/SKILL.md) |
| Text fields, pickers, sliders, toggles, selection controls | [Selection and input](subskills/apple-hig-selection-and-input/SKILL.md) |
| Progress, activity, gauges and ratings | [Status](subskills/apple-hig-status/SKILL.md) |
| Widgets, Live Activities, notifications, Siri snippets and system surfaces | [System experiences](subskills/apple-hig-system-experiences/SKILL.md) |
| Touch, keyboard, pointer, focus, eyes, gestures, controllers and sensors | [Inputs](subskills/apple-hig-inputs/SKILL.md) |
| Apple Pay, purchases, Siri, VoiceOver, AI, CarPlay and integrations | [Technologies](subskills/apple-hig-technologies/SKILL.md) |

## Apply the guidance

- **Design:** connect each important choice to the user's task and target
  platform. Include necessary interaction states, adaptation, and accessibility.
- **Implement:** prefer the project's native system components when they supply
  the needed behavior. HIG explains experience requirements; verify API names,
  availability, and code against the appropriate SDK documentation.
- **Review:** describe the observed problem, its effect, the relevant HIG rule,
  and a concrete correction. Separate source-backed findings from your own
  suggested improvements. Do not invent violations without inspecting evidence.

Include official article/section links for material recommendations. Preserve
qualifications such as “consider,” “prefer,” and “avoid”; do not turn design
advice into invented universal requirements. Retain units and platform scope for
numerical specifications. If source passages conflict, describe the conflict
and the conservative application rather than silently changing the source.

## Source boundaries

This is comprehensive local guidance, not a verbatim Apple manual or an SDK API
reference. Original media explanations are supplementary to article references;
the source page remains useful for visual demonstrations. Source snapshots and
review status live in the repository's coverage report, outside ordinary skill
loading. Do not infer that a source has been independently reviewed just because
its local file exists.

Historical `navigation-bars` links now resolve to current Toolbars guidance;
`in-app-purchase` resolves to Apple In-App Purchase. The old Touch Bar and Messages
for Business HIG pages were unavailable at this snapshot. Do not fabricate their
current rules. Translations, archived pages, and complete linked SDK/WWDC libraries
are outside the source boundary.

# Apple HIG: Inputs

Identify the device, primary input, and available accessibility alternatives. Read that input’s reference and its platform subsection before choosing gestures or control mappings. Preserve system-reserved behavior and familiar semantics; use custom interactions only where the task benefits, with discoverable alternatives and feedback. Test transitions between input methods as well as each method independently.

# Focus and selection Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/focus-and-selection) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. Focus visually identifies an interaction target for component-based navigation with keyboards, remotes, and controllers. Focus can select an item automatically, except where selection would shift context; tvOS normally requires separate activation. Rings/highlights on tablet/Mac and depth/parallax on TV reflect their platform focus models. ## Best practices Use system focus effects unless customization is essential. Do not move focus without input. If a focused item disappears during discrete directional navigation, move to a nearby one-step item; with other input, hide the indicator rather than guessing the next target. Follow platform reachability conventions: keyboard content focus on iPad/Mac coexists with Full Keyboard Access for all controls, whereas tvOS requires directional access to every interactive item. Use rings for text/search and usually full-row highlights for lists/collections. Standard focused/unfocused selection colors preserve active context. ## Platform considerations The source marks focus unsupported on iOS/watchOS in this topic’s sense. ### iPadOS Since iPadOS 15, Tab moves between focus groups and arrows move inside a group. Group custom views to produce expected reading order, normally leading-to-trailing then top-to-bottom; a vertical stack may need one focus-group container. Set priority so a likely primary item receives focus when a group is entered. Halo effects outline an item and can be refined for shape, clipping, or badge overlap. A content-configured cell’s highlighted accent appearance is separate from a focus effect. ### tvOS In full-screen content, gestures should act on the content rather than invisible focus. Use component focus for menus instead of a tiny free pointer; a gameplay-specific pointer must be conspicuous and integrated. Allow room and high-resolution art for enlarged focus states. Represent unfocused (receded), focused (raised/lit/moving), pressed (immediate feedback), selected (persistent choice such as filled favorite), and unavailable (inactive and unreachable) states distinctly. ### visionOS Connected keyboards/controllers use the same focus system family. Looking at content uses hover feedback instead; do not treat gaze hover as keyboard/controller focus. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/focus-and-selection) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: October 24, 2023, June 21, 2023.

# Remotes Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/remotes) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. The Siri Remote combines physical buttons and a touch-sensitive clickpad for tvOS navigation, selection, and playback across the room. ## Best practices Preserve standard gestures and focus direction outside specialized gameplay. Provide clear feedback connecting gesture to content. Presses indicate deliberate activation; resting/moving/passing the remote can cause accidental taps, so avoid acting on taps during live playback. Positional up/down/left/right taps can help only when intuitive and discoverable. Back normally opens the hierarchy’s parent, which is not always the previously visited screen; at the root it returns Home. During play, Back can open a pause menu to avoid accidental exits; Back from that menu resumes, while another deliberate action can return to the game menu. Holding Back reaches Home. Play/Pause must play, pause, or resume active media. ## Gestures Swipe scrolls with momentum based on swipe strength; vertical swipes along an edge accelerate through many items. Press activates or selects, and pressing before swiping enters scrubbing. ## Buttons Touch-surface swipe navigates/changes focus in apps and acts like a D-pad in games. Surface press activates/deepens navigation or acts as the game primary button. Back handles parent/exit or pause/resume according to context. Play/Pause controls media, while games may use it as a secondary action or to skip an intro. ## Compatible remotes For an app with an electronic program guide, guide/browse buttons open it; page-up/down navigate within it, also supported by upper/lower surface taps. Without an EPG, the system sends those requests to the default guide app. While content is playing, page-up/down should change channels rather than page through the guide. ## Platform considerations This source is tvOS-specific and marks the other five platforms unsupported. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/remotes) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance.

The local tvOS guidance supports separating focus from persistent selection, making every available control directionally reachable, and making unavailable controls inactive and unreachable. I’ll rank disabled destructive activation first; restoring the prior card on return will be an explicit design decision supported by the broader focus guidance.

# Apple TV project browser audit

## Scope and evidence

The supplied `interface.md` identifies tvOS and explicitly reports five behaviors. The findings below are verified against that written description, not reproduced in an application. Ranking reflects potential harm and task obstruction; frequency and actual damage are unknown.

Guidance was read locally, in this order: installed `apple-hig/SKILL.md` → `subskills/apple-hig-inputs/SKILL.md` → its routed `references/focus-and-selection.md` and `references/remotes.md`. The complete topic index was also inspected. All paths resolve within `.agents/skills/apple-hig/`. This installed Inputs family routes directly to article references; it supplies no separate topic procedure for these articles. No web access was used. Official links below identify the sources of the local snapshot, not pages checked live.

## Ranked findings and decisions

| Rank | Verified supplied behavior | Effect and correction | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 — Critical | A disabled destructive control remains activatable. | The unavailable appearance promises protection that activation does not enforce; destructive work could occur. Remove it from directional focus targets and reject activation at the action boundary whenever unavailable, including queued or stale events. | tvOS unavailable state is inactive and unreachable: [Focus and selection, tvOS](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/focus-and-selection#tvOS). Action-boundary enforcement is the proposed implementation safeguard. Actual deletion is not evidenced. |
| 2 — High | Navigation enters a dead end at a carousel boundary. | Users can become unable to continue browsing or reach another control. Define directional neighbors across carousel and surrounding regions; retain a reverse route. An outward direction at a true content edge may leave focus in place, but must not trap the user or strand available controls. | tvOS requires directional access to every interactive item: [Focus and selection, Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/focus-and-selection#Best-practices). Preserve familiar remote directions: [Remotes, Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/remotes#Best-practices). The exact broken direction and layout are not supplied. |
| 3 — High | Initial focus starts offscreen. | The current interaction target is hidden at entry. On first browser entry choose an available visible project; if none exists, choose a visible available browser action. Reveal a restored offscreen target before presenting its focus state. | Focus identifies the interaction target; tvOS uses visible component focus: [Focus and selection](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/focus-and-selection). The entry and reveal policy is a concrete design application, not a quoted initialization rule. |
| 4 — High | Focused cards look identical to selected cards. | Users cannot distinguish the next activation target from their persistent project choice. Store and render focus and selection independently; moving focus must not change the selected project. | Distinct unfocused, focused, pressed, selected and unavailable states; tvOS normally requires separate activation: [Focus and selection, tvOS](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/focus-and-selection#tvOS). |
| 5 — Medium | Returning from detail jumps to the first card. | Users lose their browsing position and must retrace navigation. Save the originating project ID, carousel and viewport; restore that card on returning to this browser. Use a deterministic nearby fallback if it no longer exists. | Restoration is a product decision consistent with avoiding unsolicited focus movement: [Focus and selection, Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/focus-and-selection#Best-practices). It is not an explicit universal restoration mandate in this snapshot. Back follows the parent hierarchy: [Remotes, Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/remotes#Best-practices). |
